attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post. The Altman reference is only an aside; the claim is his.

semantics.note: The scoreable core is the observation that hallucination was unsolved as of publication. The new-paradigm clause is hedged ('not clear'), is kept as a qualifier, and is not scored.

contract.note: The plain reading (no general solution, as opposed to reduced rates) is the ordinary meaning of 'never been a solution' and is fair to the speaker. Scoring only the historical part and leaving the hedged paradigm clause unscored is correct.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure, not an independent finding. It admits GPT-4 still hallucinates despite reductions. This is consistent with the claim, but it covers only one model.
A November 9, 2023 survey describes hallucination as a continuing, critical problem across LLMs, with mitigation still under study.
A September 2023 paper calls hallucination an unsolved issue while reporting reductions. The packet lists it as counterevidence, but it does not show elimination.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous research (e2, e3) and OpenAI's own disclosure (e1) all describe hallucination as unsolved by November 2023. Mitigation methods lowered error rates but did not eliminate hallucination. The hedged paradigm clause is not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own unhedged statement in his post.

semantics.note: 'Were never going to' is a firm, open-ended prediction that LLMs alone will not solve alignment. 'Alone' is correctly kept as a scope condition. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Requiring a validated LLM-only solution to contradict, or a covering impossibility result to support, is a fair reading of an open-ended 'never'. Elapsed time alone cannot settle the claim.

evidence.note: Anthropic disclosure (2022) of progress on harmlessness through AI feedback. This is not a validated solution to alignment.
A 2024 study shows alignment faking in one constructed scenario. It does not prove LLM-based methods can never solve alignment.
A May 2026 Anthropic disclosure reports both improvements and limits on generalisation. It neither solves alignment nor proves it impossible.
A 2025 impossibility result covers only external filtering under cryptographic assumptions. It does not cover methods that change model weights.

reviews.rationale: No item shows a validated LLM-only alignment solution, and none gives an impossibility result covering all LLM-based methods. The forecast has no deadline, so the evidence available by the cutoff does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical remark in his post.

semantics.note: A firm conditional forecast ('will'), and the antecedent about staff leaving is preserved. In context it likely referred to the threatened November 2023 exodus.

contract.note: The speaker gave no threshold for 'much' or for how many staff must leave. The contract supplies reasonable readings and correctly makes scoring depend on the antecedent occurring.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own claim that no employee was lost in November 2023 bears on the antecedent, not the outcome. It shows that episode did not trigger the forecast, so it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows no qualifying departure of OpenAI's workforce. The only item indicates no staff were lost in the 2023 crisis. With the antecedent unmet or unknown, the conditional cannot be scored, and the open horizon means nothing settles it.
